findings.F1: The tested continuation lives almost wholly in the most extreme scaled rises. On the 10-day grid, cases with a 10-day return above 2.2 of the scaled 60-day volatility were followed by +6.56 % beyond drift (t 2.30, 103 cases, 47 days). Cases in (1.5, 2.2] gave +2.43 % (t 1.18) and cases in (0.95, 1.5] gave +1.21 % (t 0.85). Inside positive values the Spearman correlation of the scaled rise with the unusual 10-day move is 0.091 (p 0.0005, 1472 cases).
findings.F2: The same continuation shows with a 30-day scaled return. Values above 1.5 were followed by +3.97 % beyond drift over 10 days (t 2.05, 311 cases, 92 days) and +5.21 % over 20 days (t 1.48, 118 cases, 39 days). At 20 days the Spearman correlation inside positive values is 0.104 (p 0.013, 568 cases). It adds no independent evidence, since it is the tested idea with a longer lookback.
findings.F3: The continuation fades with horizon. After 10-day scaled rises above 1.5, the unusual move is +1.90 % at 5 days (t 2.12) and +4.05 % at 10 days (t 2.04), but only +0.39 % at 20 days (t 0.12, 127 cases).
findings.F4: The continuation is unstable across years. After scaled rises of at least 0.9487, the unusual 10-day move was +6.2 % in 2020 and +8.7 % in 2021 but −6.5 % in 2022. Every year's t lies between −1.21 and +1.87.
findings.F5: Inside the regime, an early position looks a little better but cannot be told from chance. In its first 2 bars the unusual 10-day move is +3.26 % (t 1.94, 335 cases), against +1.98 % (t 0.78) and +2.50 % (t 0.89) later on.
findings.F6: Large scaled falls show a short rebound that does not last or grow with the fall. After a 10-day scaled fall beyond −0.9487, the unusual 5-day move is +1.65 % (t 2.12, 773 cases, 166 days) but +0.55 % at 10 days (t 0.59). After 3-day scaled falls, the strongest bin (below −1.5) gives −0.36 % (t −0.19) while the milder bin gives +1.70 % (t 1.36).
findings.F7: Close streaks themselves predict nothing on the 10-day grid. Every streak-length bin has a t between −1.39 and +1.10, from up streaks of 5 or more (+0.56 %, 111 cases) to down streaks of 5 or more (+2.07 %, 59 cases).
findings.F8: Weekday returns are positive on Fridays and Saturdays, but the pattern is concentrated in the early years. Pooled by day across coins, the mean coin return is +0.42 % on Fridays (t 2.04, 414 days) and +0.46 % on Saturdays (t 2.90). Up to 2021 the Saturday mean is +0.65 % (t 2.47); from 2022 it is +0.27 % (t 1.54), and the Friday mean is +0.24 % (t 0.91). The effect is not graded by any situation.
findings.F9: Volatility level does not change what follows. Every 20-day-volatility quintile has an unusual 10-day move between −0.49 % and +0.71 %, with every |t| under 0.7.
findings.F10: The book's gains come from the trades that stayed open. Trades held 10 days or less average −0.30 % (549 trades) and −0.82 % (896 trades), while trades of 10 to 30 days average +12.5 % and +30.7 % (397 trades each). This sorts trades after the fact rather than by anything known at a bar's close.

no_ideas: Beyond the tested idea itself (F1 to F3), the patterns I found cannot be told from chance given how many angles I looked at. These are the short rebound after scaled falls (F6, t 2.1, not graded), the Friday and Saturday returns (F8, not graded, fading after 2021) and the earlier-in-regime edge (F5, t 1.9). I also looked at streak length, volatility level, the 3-day and 30-day scaled returns, years, regime age, trade duration and entry forecast, and the book around its best and worst days, and none of them supports a new graded idea.
